lesson.subtitle: Lesson 6 -- The Performance Conversation
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato Annunciato | Lesson 6 -- The Performance Conversation

listenings.text: I have been sitting in performance conversations for eleven years, and most of the bad ones fail in the same place. They fail at the beginning. The manager opens with a soft sentence about the year in general, then a second soft sentence, and by the time the real point arrives the person has stopped listening, because they know something is coming and they are just waiting for it. A good conversation does three things and nothing else. It says what the person has been doing well, with one piece of evidence, not five. It names one area for improvement, once, in plain words, and it does not soften it away in the next sentence. And it ends with something that changes before the next review, agreed out loud by both people. Here is the part managers do not believe. Nobody has ever left a company because a manager was clear. People leave because six months of work was reviewed in four minutes by somebody who had not been paying attention.

I postponed an appraisal for four months. Not because I was busy, although that is what I told myself. I postponed it because the conversation was going to be uncomfortable, and every week it became a little more uncomfortable to have. By the time we sat down, the thing I needed to say was not news any more. It was a habit. He had been arriving late to client meetings since February, and by June the clinics had started to mention it to me instead of to him. What I learned is that the cost of waiting is never paid by the manager. It is paid by the person, who spends four months not knowing something everybody else already knows. I also learned that the same thing happens in reverse with good work. I had been thinking for months that his relationship with the hospitals was the best in the team, and I had never said it out loud. He told me afterwards that he had been considering another offer. One sentence, four months earlier, would have been enough.

extra_audio.text: Over the last six months you have been carrying the heaviest workload in the territory, and the backlog has come down from forty accounts to twelve. The one area for improvement is the weekly report, which has been arriving late since April. From now on the report goes out every Friday before six. I will hold a one-to-one with you every two weeks instead of every month.

reading.rtitle: Mid-Year Appraisal -- Sales Consultant, Interior of Sao Paulo
paras: Consultant: Marcos Ferraz. Period: January to June. Line manager: Renato Annunciato. Marcos has been covering the interior of Sao Paulo since January, and he has been working with the largest group of clinics in the territory. Over the six months of this appraisal he has reached ninety-four percent of his visit plan, and his track record on new accounts is the strongest in the team.

Three competencies are rated in this cycle. On client relationships the rating is four out of five: he has been building a strong relationship with the two teaching hospitals in Campinas, and both have asked for him by name. On planning the rating is three, because he has been running his week without a written plan and the manager has been asking for one since March. On product knowledge the rating is four.

Two milestones have been reached. The backlog of unvisited accounts has come down from forty to twelve, and the first order from the Ribeirao Preto group was signed in May. The area for improvement is reporting. Marcos has not been sending his weekly report on time, and in April and May it arrived after the regional meeting. He has not been underperforming on results, but the team cannot plan around a report that does not arrive.

The following actions have been agreed. Marcos will send the weekly report every Friday before six, and the manager will hold a one-to-one every two weeks instead of every month. If the report is late twice more in the next cycle, the manager will escalate it to the Commercial Director. The manager has acknowledged in writing that Marcos has been carrying the heaviest workload in the territory. Retention of this consultant is a priority for the region, because turnover in the interior has been high for two years.
